title: ci: three-way version coherence gate (pyproject / tag / PyPI)
body:
## What

Replaces the one-directional version-drift gate (WO-19 4.5) with a three-way coherence gate: `scripts/check_version_coherence.py` + `.github/workflows/version-coherence.yml` (PRs, pushes to main, and a **daily schedule** — a publish can fail silently after a tag is pushed, and no PR will exist to catch it). The old `version-drift.yml` is removed so exactly one version check remains.

## Assertions

| | scope | on failure |
|---|---|---|
| **A** `pyproject >= PyPI latest` | PRs + main | hard fail — the rollback check; message states the rule: *never lower a version to pass a check — bump forward instead* |
| **B** `newest release tag == PyPI latest` | main + daily | hard fail — everything tagged gets published, nothing published is untagged (the WO-19 defect class) |
| **C** `pyproject == newest tag` | main + daily | warn — legitimate mid-release state; escalates to hard fail once the bump commit is older than 7 days |

Comparisons use `packaging.version.Version`. Release tags are selected by pattern (`v<maj>.<min>.<patch>`) across all tags rather than git topology — this org carries foreign-namespace tags (`ts-sdk-v*`, `ts-types-v*`, `v1`, `*-integration`) and at least one release tag that is not an ancestor of main after a history rewrite. Repos with no tags or no PyPI release are treated as 0.0.0 with the relevant assertion skipped and noted.

## Why the old gate was insufficient

It only asked "does a tag exist for the pyproject version?" — a rollback trivially satisfies that (the *old* tag exists), which is exactly how the actenon-protocol 1.2.0 → 1.1.0 rollback passed. Both failure directions were demonstrated against the new gate before shipping (ASSERT A on a deliberately lowered version, ASSERT B on a deliberately unpublished tag).

title: Add agnostic payments adapter + Stripe reference + reconciliation (Fable 5 Part 3F)
body:
Closes Fable 5 Part 3F: the adapter wedge.

## What

First provider-backed payments adapter in the tree. Adds:

- `payments.py`: abstract `PaymentsAdapter` with payment-specific validation (integer minor units, ISO 4217, strict schemas)
- `stripe.py`: concrete `StripeAdapter` implementing refund, invoice pay, capture, cancel — with test mode and live mode
- **Reconciliation contract**: after every successful call, re-fetches the object from Stripe to confirm status/amount/currency match. Converts "provider response observed" into "provider-authenticated finality"
- 27 tests (all pass)

The adapter is provider-agnostic: `PaymentsAdapter` can be subclassed for Adyen, Braintree, GoCardless, etc.

## Verification

- 27 new tests pass
- Full permit suite: 426 passed (was 399)
- No real Stripe API calls (test_mode=True in all tests)

Refs: Fable 5 Part 3F.

title: Align Permit as the authority engine (Phase 7)
body:
## Summary

Aligns Permit as the authority engine. Permit answers: *Should authority exist for this proposed action under the configured policy and current state?* Permit must not become the protected resource boundary.

## Authority model

Pipeline: proposed action → PDP evaluation → approval/policy decision → budget reservation → grant → kernel PCCB issuance. The PDP is fail-closed. `decide_and_mint_pccb()` is the single entry point.

## Proof binding

Permit-issued proofs are now cryptographically bound to: canonical action, target, canonical parameters, audience, resource boundary, grant reference (`grant_id`), expiry, execution mode (`brokered`), operation identity (`operation_id` for Phase 6 idempotency), and attenuation constraints (via `authority_ref` digest).

New `authority_ref`: a stable SHA-256 digest of (grant_id, grant_signature, action_id, parent_grant_id, delegation_depth) that the Kernel can verify without querying Permit synchronously.

## Grant safety controls

| Control | Status |
|---|---|
| Attenuation (child ≤ parent) | ✅ enforced — widening raises ValueError |
| Delegation depth | ✅ new `delegation_depth` field (0=root, 1=child, ...) |
| Scope narrowing | ✅ child scopes must be subset of parent |
| Budget limits | ✅ child budget ≤ parent remaining |
| Time limits | ✅ child expiry ≤ parent expiry |
| Action allow-lists | ✅ via scopes.allow |
| Target allow-lists | ✅ via scopes.deny |
| One-time grants | ✅ single_use scope |
| Revocation | ✅ kill switch via `set_status(REVOKED)` |
| Revocation cascade | ✅ NEW — revoking parent cascades to children (audit P-05) |
| Approval expiry | ✅ via approval_rules + approval gate |
| Reservation release | ✅ fail-closed release on denial |
| Concurrent budget | ✅ atomic reserve/commit in SQLiteStore |

## Ledger

The hash-chained ledger records: action_type, grant_id, outcome, failure_code, reason, rule_matched, authority_boundary, est_cost, hash chain. It proves which declared process produced the authority — not that human judgement was correct.

## Compatibility impact

| Change | Breaking? |
|---|---|
| `parent_grant_id` and `delegation_depth` on Grant | No — optional with defaults |
| `authority_ref` in intent metadata | No — additive |
| `operation_id` in intent metadata | No — additive |
| Revocation cascade | Behaviour change (correct — children should be revoked when parent is) |
| uv.lock updated to kernel 0eabcdc | No — picks up Phase 6 idempotency |

## Test results

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Full permit suite | **246 passed** (was 228; +18 new independence tests) |
| Ruff | 0 errors |
| Demos (v0 + v1 gateway) | Both pass |
| TS typecheck | 0 errors |

## Residual risks

- `IdempotencyStore` is in-memory (production needs persistent store).
- `authority_ref` is not yet verified by the Kernel (the Kernel verifies the PCCB signature; `authority_ref` is metadata for audit).
- The `skills/` contamination is still present (audit P-02, out of scope for this phase).

title: Phase B — Integrate actenon-protocol v1.0.0 (pin dep, structured refusal codes, drift gate)
body:
## Summary

Integrates the pinned `actenon-protocol v1.0.0` contract into `actenon-permit`. This is **Phase B** of the four-phase integration plan documented in [actenon-protocol/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-protocol/blob/main/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md#phase-b--permit).

Phase A (kernel) is opened as [Actenon/actenon-kernel#11](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-kernel/pull/11). This PR depends on Phase A being merged first — permit imports `FailureCode` from `actenon.outcomes`, which Phase A changes to source from the protocol.

## Pinned dependency

```toml
# pyproject.toml
"actenon-protocol @ git+https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-protocol.git@v1.0.0",
```

## Changes

### `pyproject.toml` — pin protocol dep

Pins `actenon-protocol` to `v1.0.0` (was unpinned `"actenon-protocol"`).

### `src/actenon_permit/gateway.py` — surface structured refusal codes (audit P-08)

When proof verification fails at the edge, the DENY response now carries structured refusal codes per the protocol's two-layer disclosure model:

```python
return {
    "outcome": "DENY",
    "reason": f"proof verification failed at edge: {e}",
    "rule_matched": "kernel:proof_verification_failed",
    "action_id": action.action_id,
    "grant_id": grant.id,
    "remaining_budget": float(grant.budget.remaining),
    # NEW: Protocol-aligned structured refusal codes.
    "disclosed_code": disclosed_code,   # public-safe umbrella (e.g. "PROOF_INVALID")
    "internal_code": internal_code,     # detailed (null under public policy)
    "retryable": retryable,             # per the catalogue
}
```

The kernel's `ProofVerificationError.refusal_code` is mapped via the protocol's disclosure helpers (`to_disclosed_code`, `to_internal_code`, `to_retryable`). Default disclosure policy is `public` (safe for untrusted callers). This resolves audit finding P-08 (gateway swallows structured refusal_code).

### `tests/test_protocol_drift.py` — 12-test drift gate

Covers:
1. Protocol version is pinned to `1.0.0`.
2. Permit uses kernel-sourced taxonomy (transitive via `actenon.outcomes`).
3. Every refusal code the permit PDP emits is registered in the protocol catalogue.
4. Historical aliases (`PCCB_REQUIRED`, etc.) resolve deterministically to canonical codes.
5. Unknown refusal codes raise `KeyError` (not silently mapped).
6. Gateway DENY response carries `disclosed_code`, `internal_code`, `retryable` (source inspection).
7. Public-disclosed codes do not leak cryptographic detail.
8. Permit source does not import Cloud UI or tenant implementation (AST scan).
9. Protocol does not import Permit.
10. Canonicalisation byte equivalence (via the kernel's `canonical_json`).
11. Unsupported major protocol versions are rejected.
12. The transitive chain (permit → kernel → protocol) works.

### `.github/workflows/protocol-drift.yml` — CI drift gate

Runs on push, PR, and nightly. Fails on:
- Drift gate test failure.
- Missing protocol version pin in `pyproject.toml`.
- Missing structured refusal codes in the gateway DENY response (source inspection).

## Boundary preservation

Verified by `tests/test_protocol_drift.py::test_permit_does_not_import_cloud`:
- Permit's source tree does NOT import `actenon_cloud` or `app.*` (AST scan of `src/actenon_permit/`).
- The protocol package does NOT import `actenon_permit`.

Note: the test uses AST scanning rather than `sys.modules` because the cross-repo conformance test (`tests/test_cross_repo_conformance.py`) imports cloud's `ed25519_signer` for compatibility testing, which would pollute `sys.modules` in a shared test session.

## Compatibility

| Surface | Before | After | Breaking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED` | enum member (value `"PCCB_REQUIRED"`) | enum member (value `"PCCB_REQUIRED"`, `.canonical` returns `"PROOF_MISSING"`) | No |
| Gateway DENY response fields | `outcome, reason, rule_matched, action_id, grant_id, remaining_budget` | same + `disclosed_code, internal_code, retryable` | No (additive) |
| `pyproject.toml` protocol dep | `"actenon-protocol"` (unpinned) | `"actenon-protocol @ git+...@v1.0.0"` (pinned) | No (stricter) |

## Test results

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_protocol_drift.py` (new) | **12/12 passed** |
| Full permit suite | **228/228 passed** (was 216/216 before; +12 new drift gate tests) |

## Duplicate definitions removed

None directly — permit was already importing `FailureCode` from the kernel (single source of truth). This phase ensures the transitive chain (permit → kernel → protocol) is verified by the drift gate.

## Aliases retained

All 16 historical `FailureCode` enum member names are retained (via the kernel's re-export). The gateway's existing `rule_matched` field is preserved alongside the new `disclosed_code`/`internal_code` fields.

## Breaking changes

**None.** The gateway DENY response is additive (3 new fields). The `FailureCode` enum is unchanged (Phase A preserved all 16 names and values).

## After merge

- Phase C (Cloud) can begin: Cloud's `SIGNATURE_INVALID` vs `PROOF_INVALID` test drift (audit C-01) can be resolved by asserting on `disclosed_code` from the protocol.
- Phase D (Scan) is independent.

title: fix(model): enable validate_assignment on Budget for Decimal coercion
body:
Without validate_assignment, setting g.budget.remaining = 9999 (int) bypasses the _to_decimal validator and stores an int in a Decimal field, producing PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warnings during signature recomputation.

More importantly, this closes a tamper gap: without validate_assignment, g.budget.remaining = -1 would silently bypass the _non_negative validator (which only ran at init time). With validate_assignment=True, assignment also validates, so negative budget values are rejected on assignment, not just on construction.

The tamper test (test_grant_signature_roundtrip) still passes because the signature still breaks when any field changes — the fix just ensures the field is stored as Decimal, not int.
